what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Agents need behaviour, decision and workflow policies, not one
sections.para: Asking how an agent decided cannot be answered by a behaviour policy alone. The ABP says what an agent may do, an Agent Decision Policy says who chooses at a branch point and on what evidence, and an Agent Workflow Policy sets the order of steps. Zoom into one cell and it becomes both, with five states per element.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Three policies meet at fixed points and nest
sections.para: Behaviour says what an agent may do, decision who chooses and how, workflow which steps in what order; transitions are gated by decisions carried out by permitted behaviours. The ABP's approval cell zooms into its own policies, but only money, people, irreversibility and business risk justify it. Each element is defined, implemented, enforced, observed and verified separately.

sections.label: The question people ask
sections.line: Logs say what happened, not how agents decided
sections.para: With people we ask who made the call and whether they were allowed; with agents we stop at what happened. The ABP is a behaviour policy whose rows have a reach and a mandate of yes, no or approval. It cannot say who chooses between allowed actions, on what evidence or budget, so decisions need their own policy.

sections.label: Three policies
sections.line: Three policies are views of one work, not layers
sections.para: The ABP holds capabilities, reach and mandate; the Agent Decision Policy holds the decider, evidence, envelope, escalation, kill switch, sign-off and record; the Agent Workflow Policy holds states, transitions and gates. A workflow transition is gated by a decision carried out by permitted behaviours. Remove one and the others have a hole.

sections.label: Zoom into one cell
sections.line: An approval cell opens into decision and workflow policies
sections.para: In Mondweep Chakravorty's ABP merged into Ruflo's docs, delete.memory.project has reach yes and mandate approval, and since nothing can grant approval yet, approval means stop. Zoomed in, it gains a decision policy, such as the project owner approving on a verified checkpoint, and a workflow: request, verify, approve or refuse, delete, record. The shape is fractal.

sections.label: Light decisions stay inline
sections.line: Only money, people, irreversibility or risk need zooming
sections.para: Most rows never need a decision policy of their own: reading the project's files is simply yes. A row earns one when it involves money, people, irreversibility (a one-way door such as an email, deletion or payment), or a business risk a board would recognise. A hundred-row behaviour policy might need five.

sections.label: Defined is not enforced
sections.line: Five states, from defined to verified, kept separately
sections.para: Whether an element can be enforced depends on what is wired up, so each carries five states: defined, implemented, enforced, observed and verified. Observed means we can reconstruct what happened; verified, that we can prove it was right, which a complete log of a wrong refund is not. Where it is enforced matters too, from the prompt (L0) to off the machine (L4).

sections.label: Why "decision"
sections.line: Businesses sign off decisions, not workflows
sections.para: Finance runs delegation-of-authority matrices, boards keep matters reserved and the UK Corporate Governance Code asks them to set risk appetite, so "decision" links an agent's step to budget, owner and risk. OMG's DMN, adopted in 2015, already separates decisions from BPMN processes. In reinforcement learning, policy means the agent's own behaviour, the opposite of this.

sections.label: What comes next
sections.line: Three more parts: altitude, case law, scenarios mapped
sections.para: This is the first of four articles. Approve at altitude covers scaling, where each level may narrow the one above and never widen it. Case law for agents looks at how English law handles unpredicted cases, and Three decisions, mapped runs a memory, the newsroom's release and a refund through all three policies.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A proposal: only the ABP format exists today
sections.para: No Agent Decision Policy or Agent Workflow Policy format exists yet; only the ABP does. The zoomed-in decider, evidence and envelope are my illustration, not Mondweep's, and the five states are one possible cut. DMN is named to show the separation is familiar, not adopted.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: a voice memo, Mondweep's ABP and standards
sections.para: A voice memo of 17 October 2026 and the discussion with this site's agent, plus Mondweep Chakravorty's page merged into ruvnet/ruflo and mondweep/sgit-ruv-memory. Also OMG's Decision Model and Notation 1.0 of September 2015, the 2024 UK Corporate Governance Code, Principle O, and Sutton and Barto's Reinforcement Learning, second edition, section 1.3.
